About Eucalyptus

We're on a mission to make good health last a lifetime. More than 1 billion people live with obesity worldwide, driving preventable chronic conditions. We're here to build better long-term care.

Eucalyptus is now part of Hims & Hers, the global leader in personalised health and wellness.

Euc is the company behind Juniper, one of the world's largest weight-management programs combining GLP-1 medication with personalised nutrition, movement support, and clinician-led care from prescribers, nurses, health coaches, pharmacists, and dietitians. Our published clinical research shows that our combined clinical and behavioural approach helps patients lose significantly more weight during their treatment with Juniper by four times.

Our Growth Story



- 130% YoY revenue growth and a 90% reduction in cash burn - culminating in our $1.15bn acquisition by Hims & Hers in 2026, giving us the platform to take long-term care global
- Supported over 350k patients living with obesity across our 5 markets
- Received selective NICE endorsement to provide services to the NHS
- Tailored our offering to thousands of patients in Australia, the UK, Germany, Japan and Canada.


About The Role

We're looking for an Analytics Engineer to own the accuracy, reliability, and scalability of our financial data and reporting, across all of our brands.

This role sits at the intersection of finance, commercial, data, operations and engineering. You'll make sure that all of our financial models, across all of our markets, are standardised, reliable and well documented, for both internal and external reporting.

You'll work closely with the finance and commercial teams for requirements, and the engineering and operations teams globally to shape the data we collect, to produce best in class financial data models. The expectation is full end-to-end ownership: implementation, governance, data quality monitoring, and documentation. We're scaling across multiple markets, and the rigour of our financial tracking data is directly tied to the quality of decision-making within each markets, and the business’s ability to correctly allocate capital to each market.

What You'll Own

Revenue Models



- Maintain and improve the accuracy and reliability of our core orders, revenue & refunds models.
- Configure and manage integrations with financial reporting tools, eg. Netsuite.
- Standardise reporting across each region (UK, EU, AU, JP, CA).
- Partner with engineering and operations, to manage changes across products and processes, reducing downstream reporting impacts.


SEC Reporting Models



- Work with the US Hims & Hers financial team, to provide accurate, reliable and well documented data for SEC reporting.
- Build automated checks for data reliability, and monitor drift of reporting figures.
- Maintain a deep understanding of upstream source data to understand change impacts to reporting figures.


Payback Models



- Accurately model our product COGs and services costs, with our revenue data to build payback models to help inform capital allocation decisions
- Work closely with the finance, commercial and operations teams to maintain our product COGs data
- Work with the marketing teams to accurately track and attribute our marketing spend data (google, facebook, tiktok, etc)


Data quality and validation



- Monitor and validate data accuracy across financial source data
- Build automated checks for missing or duplicated data, schema drift, and anomalies
- Investigate discrepancies between source data and reported figures.
- Maintain end to end documentation of reporting models


About You



- 4-6 years in an analytics engineering, financial or commercial analytics
- Experience building / maintaining production data models
- Strong SQL skills, ideally in BigQuery, for data modelling and validation
- Detail orientated, able to self-validate assumptions and potential data gaps
- Strong sense of ownership
- Familiarity with dbt or similar transformation tools
- Familiarity with financial concepts, eg. Revenue, CAC, Payback, LTV
- Strong documentation habits — you fix things and write it down


Nice to have



- Experience with providing data for public market reporting
- Experience with financial data, Stripe, Zip, etc
- Exposure to ERP tools, eg Netsuite
- Experience with BI tools, eg Sigma


At Eucalyptus, we value individuals from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we embrace the unique qualities each person brings. When you apply, please let us know of any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. We use AI-assisted tools across our business to help our teams work more efficiently, including within our recruitment process. These tools support our team — all hiring decisions are made by real people, and every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team.

Since 2019, we’ve facilitated over one million consultations across Australia, the UK and Germany. job_title: 2026/27 CommBank Global Markets Summer Analyst Campaign
job_description:
Do work that matters 

Don’t miss this exciting opportunity to immerse yourself in CommBank’s 10-week Global Markets Summer Analyst Program (GMSA) – the perfect start to a career in Global Markets.  

Are you ready to kick start your career at one of Australia’s biggest banks? Our Global Markets team sits within Institutional Banking & Markets (IB&M) and is responsible for the Trading & Sales activities in financial markets. Being an Analyst on the program will expose you to areas such as Foreign Exchange, Commodities, Fixed Income and Interest Rate Products. 

See yourself in our team  



- Be part of a collaborative and inclusive trading floor, taking on meaningful work in a global marketplace  
- Gain exposure to a number of teams across Global Markets through dedicated learning sessions  
- Have the opportunity to receive a part-time position in Global Markets as you await your transition into a full-time role at the end of your degree (2027 commencement).  

You’ll need to be available for the full 10-week internship period from 23 November 2026 to 29 January 2027. 

In your application, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know which Global Markets team(s) you’re interested in joining and why. We’ll take your preferences into consideration however we’ll invite you to interview in the team(s) where your skills are most aligned.  

 

In the meantime, check out our website to learn more about each of the Global Markets teams. 



- Sales 
- Trading
- Commodities & Environmental Markets
- Quantitative Solutions
- CommBank iQ 

We’re interested in hearing from you if:  



- You’re passionate and curious about a career in Global Markets  
- You’re adaptable and can thrive in ever changing environments  
- You’re someone who has excellent interpersonal skills and a strong desire to succeed  

At CommBank, we’re committed to your development, career growth and training. Whether you’re from an Arts, Computer Science, French History, Economics or Mechanical Engineering background, we’d love you hear from you. 

If this sounds like you, and you are: 

If this sounds like you, and you are: 



- An Australian citizen or Australian permanent resident at the time of your application or  
- A New Zealand citizen already residing in Australia and a resident for tax purposes at the time of your application and  
- In your second-last (penultimate) year of your overall university degree and  
- Maintaining an overall minimum credit average in your degree  

Then apply now for CommBank’s GMSA Program! Applications close at

11:55pm Syd/Melb time on 13 July 2026. Successful candidates will commence in the program on 23 November 2026. 

If you're already part of the Commonwealth Bank Group (including Bankwest, x15ventures), you'll need to apply through Sidekick to submit a valid application. We’re keen to support you with the next step in your career.

We're aware of some accessibility issues on this site, particularly for screen reader users. We want to make finding your dream job as easy as possible, so if you require additional support please contact HR Direct on 1800 989 696.

Advertising End Date: 14/07/2026

job_description:
We’re BDO, a global professional services firm connected to local markets. Our people work together to provide specialist expertise, helping businesses achieve their goals.

We inspire others, to go further. We create together, to reach higher. We build trust, to lead purposefully.

Whether you're building your future or starting your career with us, you won’t do it alone. From creating solutions for our clients to building careers for our people, we shape what matters, and that’s where you come in.

About The Role

We are currently looking for an Analyst or Senior Analyst to join our Brisbane Deal Advisory team. You would be joining a large multi-disciplinary deal advisory team of around 35 professionals.

We promote a collaborative environment where our team members are encouraged to participate in a diverse range of deal advisory engagements, spanning corporate finance, valuation, due diligence, financial modelling, mergers and acquisitions, as well as infrastructure advisory.

At BDO, exceptional client service underpins our belief system and all aspects of service delivery to our clients. There are continuous opportunities to learn across each of the deal advisory service lines, build strong relationships with diverse client groups and expand networks nationally and globally at all stages of your career.

Key Responsibilities Include



- Analysing company operations and financial statements
- Completing industry research
- Using research facilities including Capital IQ to identify comparable companies and calculate relevant valuation metrics (including normalisation adjustments, as appropriate)
- Constructing, reviewing and amending financial models
- Applying valuation methodologies including discounted cash flow, capitalised maintainable earnings and option pricing models
- Writing reports in Word and PowerPoint
- Assisting with transaction management, including populating and maintaining data rooms
- Communicating with clients and other transaction advisors to progress engagements

About You



- 1+ years of experience in a professional services firm (in an area such as deal advisory/corporate finance, audit or business services) or a relevant commercial role
- Commercial acumen
- The ability to analyse and interpret financial statements (e.g. Annual Reports) to enable:

- conclusions to be formed on the financial performance and financial position of a company; and
- normalisation adjustments to be applied to compare financial performance across similar entities 
- Strong written and verbal communication skills that enable results to be communicated concisely
- The ability to devise solutions to abstract problems that have no precedent
- The ability to identify knowledge gaps and work with senior staff to develop strategies to plug these gaps
- A genuine passion for delivering exceptional client service and utilising your unique skills
- A cover letter that clearly explains why you believe you have the skills needed to succeed in this role and an understanding of BDO’s Deal Advisory team
Why BDO?

Working for BDO you will be part of a growing and market leading professional services firm.

Our national and global footprint provides our people with opportunities to work on interesting client engagements, across diverse industry sectors and services.

Our open and collaborative culture ensures access to Partners and professional mentors, to guide and accelerate your professional career, across a wide array of career pathways.

We provide our people with various health and wellbeing, social, financial, and professional development benefits to help realise what’s possible.

Participate in fitness challenges or take advantage of exclusive discounts to corporate health insurance, gym memberships and wellness facilities via our BWell program. Access benefits such as travel perks, retail discounts, employee referral rewards, study, and professional development support.

Our leave options cater to the unique needs of our people; and include enhanced family support, cultural and religious leave, and options to purchase additional leave. You can also give back and get involved in community initiatives via our BCaring program.

With a strong focus on learning and growth, we provide on the job training and formal development programs to help you succeed in your role and develop your skills and experience.

Our culture is underpinned by our core values (One, Bold, Human, Heart and Strive).

We are proud to be recognised as an Inclusive Employer for 2025-2026 by Diversity Council of Australia and a  2024-2025 Employer of Choice for Gender Equality by the Workplace Gender Equality Agency (WGEA).

BDO is committed to inclusive and accessible recruitment practices. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support your application or interview process, we encourage you to contact our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@bdo.com.au

About The Business



- Learning and Development Opportunities
- Secure opportunity with a Tier 1 Mining Asset 
- Live in the award winning, family friendly Mid-Western Region

We are Australia’s largest pure-play coal producer generating over $10 billion in Foreign Direct Investment; owning, operating or participating in coal mines across NSW, Queensland and Western Australia.

Moolarben Coal mine is Australia’s largest thermal coal producer and has both Underground and Open cut operations producing over 21 million tpa. It has over 800 employees with employees residing in the beautiful Mudgee area, with all the facilities for a fantastic family lifestyle.

Job Tasks And Responsibilities

Reporting to the Commercial Superintendent, you will be responsible for:



- Assisting with Monthly management reporting, educating end users of the accounting system with awareness and understanding of processes applicable to the accounting modules.
- Manage the Asset Register to ensure all assets are accounted for.
- Reconcile Asset Register on a quarterly basis.
- Provide cost reporting analysis to managers and supervisors with transparency of costs.
- Facilitate cost review meetings with department managers and supervisors.
- Administer and control project/CAPEX applications in line with policy and use of the accounting system.
- Assist with the preparation of financial statements with notes to Join Venture stage where appropriate.
- Ensure trial balance reconciliations are completed.
- Applying data science techniques to forecast production costs and identify operational risks.

Skills And Experience

Essential Criteria:



- Tertiary qualifications in accounting or related field (or working towards).
- Previous experience in commercial accounting roles.
- Management accounting experience in the resource sector (desirable).
- Experience with SAP accounting system (desirable).
- Proficient in using Microsoft Suite of products and accounting software.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.
- Exposure to machine learning or advanced analytics techniques.
- Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with all stakeholders.

Benefits

Yancoal provides a range of benefits to appeal to the diverse needs of our employees. The following benefits are available to eligible employees:



- Salary continuance and life insurance
- Paid parental leave
- Subsidised private health insurance 
- Fitness Passport - discounted workplace health and fitness program
- Study assistance
- Flexible work arrangements
- Employee Assistance Program
- Access to financial education and banking discounts 
- Salary packaging including novated leasing and remote area benefits
- Service recognition rewards
- Discounts program including major department stores, cinemas, restaurants

Yancoal Australia values diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from people with diverse backgrounds including First Nations people, people with disability, people from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds, and people that identify as LGBTQIA+.

If this sounds like the opportunity you've been looking for, apply today and take the first step toward an exciting new journey with us!

If you have any concerns regarding the authenticity of communications received representing Yancoal, please email recruitment@yancoal.com.au with the subject “Fraud Query”, outlining your concern.

Forensic Accountant – Assistant Manager / Senior Consultant
Leading Advisory Firm | Melbourne CBD


Join a leading specialist advisory firm working on complex, high-value matters where your analysis directly impacts real commercial outcomes.
This is an excellent opportunity for an Auditor looking to transition into forensic accounting, or an existing forensic accounting professional seeking broader exposure to valuations and disputes work. Full training and mentoring will be provided.


In this role, you’ll build on your audit and financial analysis experience by:

- Conducting detailed financial investigations, damages assessments and business valuations.
- Analysing complex accounting issues and applying your knowledge of financial reporting in a disputes and litigation context.
- Building advanced financial models in Excel, including discounted cash flow (DCF) analyses.
- Contributing to clear, well-structured expert reports that assist courts and parties in understanding the financial issues in a case.
- Working closely with leading litigation lawyers and recognised expert witnesses on high-profile matters.
- Developing strong professional relationships and laying the groundwork to become an expert witness in the future.


Why this will appeal

- Clear pathway from Audit into Forensic Accounting
- Strong exposure to valuations and financial modelling
- Work on complex, high-value matters across disputes and investigations
- Direct mentoring from experienced forensic specialists
- Supportive, high-performing team within a global firm


Who they’re looking for

- 2–4 years’ experience in External Audit or Forensic Accounting
- CA qualified (or near completion)
- Strong Excel skills with exposure to financial modelling
- Interest in valuations, investigations or disputes work
- Strong communication and report-writing skills


Salary: circa $125,000 package
Eligibility: Full Australian working rights required.


Keen to know more?
Contact Helen Cramp at Troy Recruitment on 0413 198 073 or helen@troyrecruitment.com,
or connect on LinkedIn.

- Insolvency Accountant position available in Newcastle
- Great Culture and fun environment
- Career pathway and progression 
Working with businesses that are in distress is challenging. But, as advisers, we have the opportunity to help business owners and people affected by a potential insolvency to minimize the damage and, in some cases, revive a failing business.
Due to growth, we are seeking a Senior to Supervisor level Accountant to join our Restructuring, Turnaround & Insolvency Team. To be a success you’ll need to have excellent organisational and time management skills, be well presented and self-motivated.
We work with people from all walks of life and across various industries. Our perfect candidate will be a quick learner, have excellent written and verbal communication skills and be familiar with Xero, MYOB, Quickbooks, Microsoft Excel, Word and Outlook. In insolvency, we are dealing with people at a highly emotive time in their lives and resilience and empathy are key traits that we’re looking for in our new recruit.
In return, we’ll offer you access to industry leaders to learn from. Our people have vast experience at managing corporate and personal insolvencies as well as rescuing failing businesses and getting them back on their feet and will teach you how to become an expert in your trade.
To be considered for the position, you’ll need:

- To be confident, professional and have a team focused approach, able to work productively with all levels in the team from graduate to partner
- Experienced within insolvency/restructuring/bankruptcy
- A relevant university degree
- Completed or undertaking qualifications CA/CPA and ARITA

About Us

At Transgrid, our work improves the lives of millions – from lighting up sports fields, schools and homes, to powering the wheels of commerce and everything else in between. Now it’s your turn to make it happen.

We play a crucial role in delivering safe, reliable, and sustainable energy to millions of Australians. Operating over 13,000 km of high-voltage transmission lines and 128 substations across NSW and the ACT, we connect electricity generators to the distribution network powering homes, businesses, and communities. As Australia accelerates its energy transition, the work we do has never been more significant.

At Transgrid, we're playing a critical role in Australia's clean energy future. As we deliver the infrastructure that connects renewable energy projects and powers millions of homes, businesses and communities across NSW and the ACT, we're looking for a skilled Project Accountant to join our team.

In this role, you'll provide trusted financial support across major infrastructure projects, ensuring accurate financial reporting, robust analysis and valuable insights that enable informed decision-making. Working closely with project teams and stakeholders across the business, you'll help drive financial performance, reporting integrity and continuous improvement throughout the project lifecycle.

About You

You're a detail-oriented Project Accountant with experience supporting large-scale infrastructure or capital projects. You enjoy partnering with stakeholders, analysing financial data and providing meaningful insights that help projects succeed.

You'll Bring



-  Degree qualifications in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline. 
-  Experience in project accounting within a large corporate or infrastructure environment. 
-  Strong financial accounting, reporting, analytical and financial modelling skills. 
-  The ability to interpret complex financial data and communicate insights to a range of stakeholders. 
-  Experience driving business performance and continuous process improvement. 
-  Advanced Microsoft Excel skills. 
-  Excellent stakeholder management, communication and relationship-building skills. 
-  Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines. 
-  Knowledge of accounting standards, regulatory frameworks, and asset cost accounting/capitalisation (desirable). 

 Our Leadership Principles & Values 

Our Leadership Principles, Courage, Care, Clarity and Connection, form the foundation of how we lead at Transgrid. Courage means doing what is right even when it is hard. Care means valuing people and leading with genuine consideration for others. Clarity means making sure your team understands what good looks like and why their work matters. Connection means linking people to our purpose and building strong relationships across teams, customers and partners.

You will also uphold our Values: Safety, Achievement, Integrity and Service, delivering outcomes that are safe, sustainable and genuinely useful to the customers and communities we serve.

At Transgrid, we empower our people with a well-rounded benefits package designed to support their personal, professional and social wellbeing, helping them deliver their best work every day.



-  20 Weeks Paid Parental Leave : Genuine support for every stage of family life. 
-  Corporate Discounts : Retail, utilities, travel, health and wellbeing, and more. 
-  Novated Leasing : Tax-effective vehicle options through novated leasing arrangements. 
-  Workplace Flexibility : Work from home flexibility and flexible arrangements to suit your life and your role. 
-  Tertiary Education Support : Financial support for ongoing study and professional development. 
-  Career Mentoring and Training : Regular training and career mentoring to help you grow. 

 Applications close on Monday, July 20th  however will be assessed on a rolling basis and may close earlier – Apply today and play a crucial role in driving the transition to a cleaner, more sustainable energy future!

Transgrid is committed to Health and Safety, the Environment, Equal Employment Opportunity, Diversity and Ethical Practices. All applicants are expected to demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to these areas.

The company
Fiable is an innovative technology company with employees spread across Australia and the Philippines, with exciting plans underway to expand into the UK market. Our platform provides contractors in the built environment with real-time insights into subcontractor delivery risk, helping them make informed decisions about the suppliers they engage. 


As the Commercial Finance and Assessment Director, you will lead and scale our global financial assessment capability, ensuring exceptional service delivery, operational excellence, and high-quality assessment outcomes as we continue to grow. Working closely with the COO, Product, Technology and Commercial teams, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping the future of our assessment function through innovation, automation and continuous improvement, helping deliver trusted financial insights that underpin Fiable's reputation for integrity, transparency and customer confidence.


We're growing fast, loved by customers, and building a brand that solves real-world problems.


The opportunity
The Commercial Finance and Assessment Director is responsible for leading Fiable’s end-to-end Financial Viability Assessment function across multiple geographies. This role owns global service delivery, workforce strategy, operational excellence, and transformation of Fiable’s assessment capability at scale.


This is a fully remote position (must be located in Australia) that oversees all teams that work together globally to deliver our assessments, ensuring consistent, high-quality outputs while adapting to regional requirements and growth dynamics. As a key member of the operations leadership team, this role drives long-range capacity planning, operational scalability, and strategic transformation initiatives, including SaaS enablement and product expansion.


This is a highly strategic yet hands-on leadership role, requiring deep financial and commercial acumen, global team leadership experience, and the ability to step into critical operational functions when needed.


What we need

- Qualified Chartered Accountant
- Have held a Commercial Finance role or the like within the Construction sector or similar.
- Extensive experience in financial analysis, operations leadership, or assessment-based environments, ideally at regional or global scale.
- Demonstrated success leading distributed or multi-geography teams.
- Strong expertise in workforce planning, capacity modelling, and operational scaling.
- Proven track record delivering transformation initiatives (e.g., SaaS, automation, or digital platforms).
- Deep understanding of financial documentation, risk assessment, and analytical processes.
- Strategic mindset with a hands-on, execution-focused approach.
- Exceptional stakeholder management and executive communication skills
- High adaptability in fast-paced, high-growth environments.


What does success look like in this role

- Global assessment operations scales seamlessly with growth while maintaining quality and turnaround times.
- Workforce supply consistently meets demand with minimal volatility or service risk.
- Transformation initiatives materially improve productivity, cost efficiency, and customer experience.
- Teams operate with strong engagement, accountability, and clear performance standards.
- The function is recognised internally and externally as a best-in-class financial assessment capability.
- The positive culture and employee wellbeing of all employees is a key priority.  


For the opportunity to be a part of this exciting journey APPLY NOW with a cover letter detailing your relevant experience to the role or call Sarah for more information on 0417 465 019.

Job Description


Position: Commercial Planning & Category Manager


Location: Melbourne, Australia


Department: Commercial


Reports to: Head of Commercial – ANZ


Employment Type: Permanent, full-time


Role Purpose


The Commercial Planning & Category Manager is a hands-on analytical and commercial role, sitting at the intersection of finance, data and FMCG category management for Lifestyles Healthcare ANZ.


You will own demand forecasting, financial modelling and performance reporting, while applying those capabilities to real commercial problems – category growth, customer planning, and retail execution.


This is an ideal opportunity for finance or analytics professional with 3–5 years’ experience who has built strong modelling and data skills and is looking to apply them in a fast-moving consumer goods environment.


An understanding of FMCG or the Australian retail landscape is valued, but your analytical foundation is what will set you apart.


Key Accountabilities
Strategic Planning & Commercial Forecasting

- Own the rolling short-, mid- and long-range forecasts (volume, value, mix), including risks & opportunities and scenario modelling aligned to business targets.
- Support the annual operating plan and contribute to long-range planning, translating market and internal performance trends into actionable strategies.
- Partner with Finance to ensure forecast integrity, P&L transparency, and alignment of top-line and margin objectives.


Category Management & Retailer Engagement

- Use scan data, shopper insights and category tools to analyses category performance, identify growth opportunities, and contribute to category strategies and customer plans across key retail channels.
- Support range reviews, assortment optimization, pricing/promo strategies, and NPD launches in partnership with Category, Sales and Marketing.
- Embed shopper-led insights into customer conversations to influence retailer decisions and in-store execution (e.g., shelf, space, and promotional mechanics).


Financial Modelling & Performance Management

- Build robust financial models to evaluate initiatives (e.g., NPD, channel expansion, media/promo investments), including sensitivity analysis and ROI.
- Track and analyses KPIs (revenue, NSV, GP, mix, market share, promo ROI), generating clear insights and corrective actions.
- Develop well-structured business cases with clear assumptions, dependencies, and measurable outcomes to support internal decision making.


Demand/Supply Integration (S&OP / IBP)

- Contribute to monthly demand reviews, supporting alignment across Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain and Finance.
- Improve forecast accuracy, service levels and inventory health through exception management and continuous improvement.
- Support scenario planning for supply constraints, portfolio changes, and customer initiatives.


Data, Analytics & Tools

- Use syndicated data platforms (e.g., Circana, IRI, or similar) to build category and customer reports, manage item data integrity, and create repeatable insight assets.
- Synthesize syndicated POS, shopper panel, and customer portal data with internal ERP and finance data to create a single version of the truth.
- Design automated dashboards and self-serve views in Power BI/Tableau; champion data quality, governance and documentation.


Communication, Stakeholder Management & Storytelling

- Communicate analysis clearly and concisely, translating data into commercial recommendations for cross-functional teams and customers.
- Collaborate effectively across Sales, Marketing, Finance and Supply Chain to support cross-functional alignment and decision making.
- Prepare clear business reporting and customer-ready sell-in materials to support sales conversations and internal performance reviews.


Qualifications & Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Marketing, Data Analytics or a related field.
- 3–5 years’ experience in a finance, analytics or commercial planning role; backgrounds in commercial finance, FP&A, demand planning, category insights or trade marketing are all relevant. Experience in FMCG or with major Australian retailers is advantageous but not essential.
- Strong financial modelling skills in Excel, with solid experience in forecasting methodologies, scenario analysis and working with P&L data.
- Exposure to syndicated data platforms such as Circana, IRI or similar; familiarity with retailer data portals is a plus.
- Proficiency with analytics and visualization tools (Power BI/Tableau) and strong data storytelling skills.
- Some familiarity with ERP or BI systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle) and an understanding of S&OP or demand planning processes is beneficial but not essential.


Capabilities & Behaviours

- Analytically strong with a natural curiosity about commercial performance – comfortable moving between financial models and category or market data.
- Analytical problem-solver with high attention to detail and a bias for action.
- Influential communicator who can simplify complexity and align stakeholders around clear decisions.


Success Measures (Role KPIs)

- Forecast accuracy and bias (volume and value) and adherence to S&OP/IBP rhythms.
- Delivery of category and customer growth outcomes (e.g., share, NSV, GM, promo ROI).


Application Process

- Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your experience in financial modelling, forecasting or analytics, and how you have applied those skills to drive commercial outcomes – ideally in an FMCG or retail context.
- Shortlisted candidates will complete a case study focused on category diagnosis and forecasting.

LifeStyles has a history dating back to 1905 when Eric Ansell first started making condoms in Richmond Australia.


Today LifeStyles is a Global leader in the sexual wellness sector, comprising a broad range of condoms, personal lubricants, and other related products and other products in over 60 countries.


The LifeStyles family of brands includes the #1 global non-latex condom brand, SKYN®, Owning a large portfolio of trademarks, LifeStyles manufactures and commercialises its products, under its local heroes such as Mates®, LifeStyles®, Manix®, Unimil®, and Blowtex® and Control. LifeStyles owns and operates manufacturing facilities in Thailand, India and Spain, and it employs over 1,600 teammates globally.


LifeStyles Healthcare was created on September 1, 2017, when the consortium of Humanwell Healthcare & CITIC Capital private equity purchased the Sexual Wellness division from Ansell.


As of December 1, 2022, Lifestyles is owned by Linden Capital Partners, a Chicago-based private equity firm focused on the healthcare industry.


This is an exciting time to join us. We combine century-long history with the opportunity of a new beginning as a stand-alone company - this means a new way of thinking, the opportunity to explore new horizons and the chance to make a mark in an exciting, fresh business.

We are empowered professionals, and we are committed to creating a team of the world’s “best of the best.” Our business foundation is strong, among our values are Integrity and Respect, our people are highly engaged. We have a focus on safety and teamwork - and we want you to join us! If you're looking for a daring opportunity to build brands in this booming & thrilling category, then let's talk.

You will own demand forecasting, financial modelling and performance reporting, while applying those capabilities to real commercial problems – category growth, customer planning, and retail execution.


This is an ideal opportunity for finance or analytics professional with 3–5 years’ experience who has built strong modelling and data skills and is looking to apply them in a fast-moving consumer goods environment.


An understanding of FMCG or the Australian retail landscape is valued, but your analytical foundation is what will set you apart.


Key Accountabilities

Strategic Planning & Commercial Forecasting

  • Own the rolling short-, mid- and long-range forecasts (volume, value, mix), including risks & opportunities and scenario modelling aligned to business targets.
  • Support the annual operating plan and contribute to long-range planning, translating market and internal performance trends into actionable strategies.
  • Partner with Finance to ensure forecast integrity, P&L transparency, and alignment of top-line and margin objectives.


Category Management & Retailer Engagement

  • Use scan data, shopper insights and category tools to analyses category performance, identify growth opportunities, and contribute to category strategies and customer plans across key retail channels.
  • Support range reviews, assortment optimization, pricing/promo strategies, and NPD launches in partnership with Category, Sales and Marketing.
  • Embed shopper-led insights into customer conversations to influence retailer decisions and in-store execution (e.g., shelf, space, and promotional mechanics).


Financial Modelling & Performance Management

  • Build robust financial models to evaluate initiatives (e.g., NPD, channel expansion, media/promo investments), including sensitivity analysis and ROI.
  • Track and analyses KPIs (revenue, NSV, GP, mix, market share, promo ROI), generating clear insights and corrective actions.
  • Develop well-structured business cases with clear assumptions, dependencies, and measurable outcomes to support internal decision making.


Demand/Supply Integration (S&OP / IBP)

  • Contribute to monthly demand reviews, supporting alignment across Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain and Finance.
  • Improve forecast accuracy, service levels and inventory health through exception management and continuous improvement.
  • Support scenario planning for supply constraints, portfolio changes, and customer initiatives.


Data, Analytics & Tools

  • Use syndicated data platforms (e.g., Circana, IRI, or similar) to build category and customer reports, manage item data integrity, and create repeatable insight assets.
  • Synthesize syndicated POS, shopper panel, and customer portal data with internal ERP and finance data to create a single version of the truth.
  • Design automated dashboards and self-serve views in Power BI/Tableau; champion data quality, governance and documentation.


Communication, Stakeholder Management & Storytelling

  • Communicate analysis clearly and concisely, translating data into commercial recommendations for cross-functional teams and customers.
  • Collaborate effectively across Sales, Marketing, Finance and Supply Chain to support cross-functional alignment and decision making.
  • Prepare clear business reporting and customer-ready sell-in materials to support sales conversations and internal performance reviews.


Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Marketing, Data Analytics or a related field.
  • 3–5 years’ experience in a finance, analytics or commercial planning role; backgrounds in commercial finance, FP&A, demand planning, category insights or trade marketing are all relevant. Experience in FMCG or with major Australian retailers is advantageous but not essential.
  • Strong financial modelling skills in Excel, with solid experience in forecasting methodologies, scenario analysis and working with P&L data.
  • Exposure to syndicated data platforms such as Circana, IRI or similar; familiarity with retailer data portals is a plus.
  • Proficiency with analytics and visualization tools (Power BI/Tableau) and strong data storytelling skills.
  • Some familiarity with ERP or BI systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle) and an understanding of S&OP or demand planning processes is beneficial but not essential.


Capabilities & Behaviours

  • Analytically strong with a natural curiosity about commercial performance – comfortable moving between financial models and category or market data.
  • Analytical problem-solver with high attention to detail and a bias for action.
  • Influential communicator who can simplify complexity and align stakeholders around clear decisions.


Success Measures (Role KPIs)

  • Forecast accuracy and bias (volume and value) and adherence to S&OP/IBP rhythms.
  • Delivery of category and customer growth outcomes (e.g., share, NSV, GM, promo ROI).


Application Process

  • Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your experience in financial modelling, forecasting or analytics, and how you have applied those skills to drive commercial outcomes – ideally in an FMCG or retail context.
  • Shortlisted candidates will complete a case study focused on category diagnosis and forecasting.

LifeStyles has a history dating back to 1905 when Eric Ansell first started making condoms in Richmond Australia.


Today LifeStyles is a Global leader in the sexual wellness sector, comprising a broad range of condoms, personal lubricants, and other related products and other products in over 60 countries.


The LifeStyles family of brands includes the #1 global non-latex condom brand, SKYN®, Owning a large portfolio of trademarks, LifeStyles manufactures and commercialises its products, under its local heroes such as Mates®, LifeStyles®, Manix®, Unimil®, and Blowtex® and Control. The brands values are centered around sex positivity, pleasure, confidence and inclusivity.


Outside of branded products, the Company also supports universities, NGOs, and other organizations as part of a broader effort to promote sexual health and prevent the spread of STDs and STIs. LifeStyles owns and operates manufacturing facilities in Thailand, India and Spain, and it employs over 1,600 teammates globally.


LifeStyles Healthcare was created on September 1, 2017, when the consortium of Humanwell Healthcare & CITIC Capital private equity purchased the Sexual Wellness division from Ansell.


As of December 1, 2022, Lifestyles is owned by Linden Capital Partners, a Chicago-based private equity firm focused on the healthcare industry.


This is an exciting time to join us. We combine century-long history with the opportunity of a new beginning as a stand-alone company - this means a new way of thinking, the opportunity to explore new horizons and the chance to make a mark in an exciting, fresh business.


LifeStyles Healthcare is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.


We are empowered professionals, and we are committed to creating a team of the world’s “best of the best.” Our business foundation is strong, among our values are Integrity and Respect, our people are highly engaged. We have a focus on safety and teamwork - and we want you to join us! If you're looking for a daring opportunity to build brands in this booming & thrilling category, then let's talk.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Our client is a global leader in aviation services, supporting airlines and airports across more than 40 countries. In Australia and New Zealand, the business operates a large, operationally intensive network where finance plays a critical role in supporting commercial performance, operational excellence and disciplined financial management.


Based in Mascot in Sydney and reporting directly to the CFO, this is a broad Financial Controller role with responsibility for leading finance across Australia and New Zealand. You'll lead an established team spanning Financial Reporting, Financial Control, and Finance Business Partnering, with the opportunity to influence financial performance across a complex multi-site operation.


While backed by the scale, systems and best practice of a global organisation, the ANZ business enjoys genuine local ownership. You'll work closely with the executive leadership team, partnering with operational stakeholders, and playing an active role in shaping financial outcomes across the region.


Key responsibilities include:

- Lead the ANZ finance team across Financial Reporting, Financial Control and Finance Business Partnering
- Oversee statutory and management reporting, balance sheet integrity and financial governance
- Ensure compliance with IFRS, tax and regulatory requirements across Australia and New Zealand
- Drive strong financial controls, governance and continuous improvement across finance processes
- Partner with operational leaders to provide commercial insight and support strategic decision-making
- Develop and mentor a high-performing finance leadership team while working closely with regional and global stakeholders


The successful candidate will likely be CA/CPA qualified (Chartered or Big 4 trained) and bring strong Financial Controller or senior finance leadership experience within a large private or multinational organisation. You'll combine strong technical accounting capability with the commercial judgement and leadership style required to influence stakeholders across a dynamic operational business.


This is an outstanding opportunity to join a recognised global leader in a role offering genuine breadth, executive exposure and the autonomy to make a tangible impact across the ANZ business.


Applicants must have full working rights in Australia.


For a confidential discussion, please contact Michael Nolan on 02 9235 9460 mnolan@jmes.com.au

Our mission is to ensure no senior professional remains invisible in the global remote market, not because they lack the skills, but because the system failed to read them correctly.
